 XRP spot exchange-traded funds pulled in $8.43 million on Oct. 29, their biggest daily net inflow in October, ending four straight sessions of net outflows. Franklin Templeton’s XRPZ accounted for $5.57 million and the Bitwise XRP ETF added $2.86 million, while other products saw no flows. October cumulative net inflows stood at about $19.33 million, down 84% from September.

 XRP spot exchange-traded funds (ETFs) pulled in $8.43 million on Oct. 29, the biggest daily net inflow so far in October 2026.
 Blockchain outlet The Crypto Basic reported on Oct. 30 that the inflow ended four straight trading sessions of net outflows and marked the first daily gain since Oct. 23.
 XRP spot ETFs have seen little new money recently, but buying returned on Oct. 29. Still, it is difficult to conclude that investor sentiment has shifted based on a one-day rebound. XRP remains under price pressure, and it needs to be seen whether ETF demand will continue.
 By product, Franklin Templeton’s XRPZ drew the most, with $5.57 million. The Bitwise XRP ETF posted net inflows of $2.86 million. The two products accounted for all of the day’s inflows, and other products including Canary Capital’s XRPC had no inflows or outflows.
 The Oct. 29 inflow of $8.43 million was above Oct. 8’s $8.17 million, the previous high for October. But the broader monthly trend still shows a limited recovery. Cumulative net inflows for October were about $19.33 million, down 84% from September’s $121.40 million. Compared with August’s $158.18 million, the decline reaches 87%.
 Flows within the ETF market were mixed. Ethereum, BNB, Solana and TRON-related ETFs had no net inflows on the same day. Bitcoin spot ETFs, by contrast, drew $17.07 million.
 Among altcoin ETFs, only XRP spot ETFs and Zcash spot ETFs recorded net inflows. Ethereum spot ETFs posted net outflows of $105.48 million, and Solana spot ETFs also saw $27.69 million leave.
 The figures show ETF money has not fully exited despite XRP’s weak price. With a one-day rebound and a slowdown in monthly inflows occurring together, future fund flows are expected to determine whether demand is actually recovering.
